coursename: SWRK 9100 Quantitative Research Methods
coursedescription: The purpose of this course is to teach the basics of practice research, with an emphasis on intervention research and answering practice questions. This course will focus on research ethics, building conceptual frameworks, source credibility, formulation of research questions and hypotheses, various designs, sampling methods, operationalization of concepts and measurement issues, and various scale types and scale selection criteria. Special emphasis will be placed on the development of designing feasible and practical research studies to answer questions of importance to social work practice. The course will cover the selection and development of outcome measures, intervention manuals, and fidelity measures. It will examine evidence-based practice and its relationship to systematic reviews and meta-analysis. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9120 Qualitative Research Methods
coursedescription: The purpose of this course is to introduce doctoral students to the philosophical and methodological issues of qualitative research. Students will learn about the array of qualitative approaches (such as grounded theory, narrative research, and case study) and will focus heavily on procedures such as generating a research question, gathering data, coding, memo writing, analysis/interpretation, and writing that are common to most approaches. In addition, students will consider ethical issues unique to qualitative research and the role of researcher reflexivity. Students will also learn about standards for good qualitative research and how to assess a piece of qualitative research. This will be a “hands-on” class, with a focus on understanding and practicing basic skills with the goal of producing a qualitative proposal and becoming an informed consumer of qualitative research. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring Prerequisite: SWRK 9100 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9130 Clinical Theory I
coursedescription: The purpose of this course is to broaden and deepen participants' mastery of several theories of development, personality, and behavior that have contributed to social work's knowledge base across the decades and continue to inform clinical social work epistemology today. Drawing primarily from original sources, we will study the evolution of theories central to psychodynamic thought, from Freud's early biological model of the mind, through various relational perspectives, to contemporary work in the fields of attachment and interpersonal neurobiology. The course will also cover the paradigm shift to first- through third-wave cognitive-behavioral theories and explore the potential for psychodynamically-informed cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT). We will consider key assumptions, constructs, and propositions of each theory in terms of its congruence with social work's principles, values, and mission and in relation to the profession's person-in-environment perspective. This process will involve critically examining the empirical support and indications for the use of various psychotherapy practices. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9140 Clinical Theory II
coursedescription: This course reviews contemporary theories of Couples and Family Therapy within a historical perspective. Family approaches reviewed include systemic, structural, experiential, attachment-based, narrative, and psycho-educational models. Couples models include the Gottman Method, Emotionally-Focused Couples Work, Imago, and Cognitive Behavioral Work. Case studies, films, and critical discussions will be used to deepen students’ understanding of different models. The course will also include an understanding of economic constraints, cultural differences, sexual orientation, and larger systemic influences. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring Prerequisite: SWRK 9130 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9150 Dissertation Seminar
coursedescription: A dissertation is an independent work of scholarship that explores a topic of expertise in depth. Ideally, it can be disseminated in the academic literature to advance the body of knowledge in a given area. This workshop is designed to consider the various types of studies that can be used for the dissertation and how to complete it in the next three years. It will also cover the dissertation team and how to select a chair that will help you cross the finish line. Finally the parts of the proposal will be addressed, with some detail given to the literature review and the place of systematic reviews within that. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9170 Applied Statistics
coursedescription: This course is designed to provide students with a range of statistical methods and applications used for research in human services and clinical practice settings. Topics covered include types of measurement and variables, and basic concepts and techniques for exploring and categorizing data, for generalizing data from sample to population and tests of significance. An emphasis will be placed on the practical applications of data to address social work practice issues. Students will learn how to choose and apply statistical tools to data sources, when and how statistical tools can be used to analyze data, and how to interpret others' quantitative studies. Students will gain hands-on experience in using windows-based statistical software to manage and analyze quantitative data. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9180 Trauma Interventions
coursedescription: Given the prevalence of trauma and its long-lasting effects, professionals in social work and behavioral health frequently encounter individuals seeking support for trauma-related challenges. This course focuses on equipping practitioners with an advanced understanding of trauma-informed assessment, treatment interventions, and resilience-based services. Students will explore the complexities of trauma treatment, including managing challenges and crises, addressing common countertransference and reenactment dynamics, understanding the impact of vicarious traumatization, and fostering post-traumatic growth in both clients and practitioners. The course will also emphasize the importance of considering the client’s context, intersectionality, and cultural background, as well as addressing social justice issues related to trauma causation, consequences, and healing. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9190 Teaching Social Work Practice
coursedescription: Teaching Social Work Practice focuses on the critical elements of teaching social work practice. It presents teaching as a scholarly endeavor that integrates and synthesizes knowledge, skills, values, creativity, and reflection in the planning and transmission of professional comportment, content, and processes in social work education. While the primary focus is on practice courses, the material covered can be used to prepare students for teaching in other curricular areas. An emphasis will be on acquiring knowledge of the goals of social work education and professional development and how these goals inform what and how we teach. Course participants will identify, discuss, and address their unique characteristics and their real and anticipated teaching challenges in the classroom environment. We will build on participants’ strengths, examine, and apply diverse teaching strategies for students with various learning approaches and experiences. Participants will learn how to plan courses by critically applying principles of teaching and learning, lesson organization, as well as incorporating their own unique professional and personal attributes. Different approaches to student assessment will be discussed. In addition, teacher evaluation, an essential aspect of the educational process, will be examined. Students will also learn the essentials of writing a teaching philosophy statement. This course is intended to be interactive, stimulating, and thought provoking. There will be opportunities to practice the application of various teaching techniques and methods discussed from the readings and other resources. We will offer genuine critique and feedback of each other’s contributions in a supportive and open environment with the goal of facilitating your professional development as instructors. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Fall 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9200 Advanced Topics in Social Work Practice
coursedescription: Topics vary. The second and final year of DSW coursework culminates in two electives selected by the student cohort completed as a group. Previous topics include: Neurophysiology of Trauma, Substance Use Interventions, Introduction to Sex Therapy, Clinical Practice with Adolescents and Young Adults, Ethics in Mental Health Care, Trauma Informed Supervision and Leadership for Change. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring 0.25-1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9210 American Racism, Patriarchy, Intersectionality, and Social Work Practice
coursedescription: This course explores the complexities of inequity in America: the construction of racial and ethnic categories, the impact of inequity on identity, individuals and social institutions, and the influence of ideology and oppressive policies and practices on social welfare systems and their clients. This course will also examine overlapping or intersecting social identities and related systems of oppression, domination, or discrimination (Crenshaw, 1991). Students will use an intersectional lens to consider inequity and consider how the historical and contemporary experiences of African American, Indigenous, Latinx, Asian, LGBTQ+, disabled, and other marginalized groups are best understood. The examination of historical aspects of bias against marginalized groups informs inquiry into contemporary policies and practices including housing, education, environmental justice, economics, employment, politics, religion, and immigration. We will discuss the assigned scholarship, and consider the congruence of the policies and practices with the ethics and values of clinical social work, and the social work profession more broadly. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9230 Social Construction and Social Work Practice: Transforming Dialogues
coursedescription: This course focuses on the application of a social constructionist orientation to social work practice and inquiry with an emphasis on its transforming potential. Using critical analyses and dialogue, we will examine traditional and contemporary issues germane to social work and explore how assumptions and dominant understandings of these issues influence policies, practice, and inquiry. Our explorations will be informed by readings, dialogue, presentations, and reflexive/reflective/analytical writing. Relevant contexts will include your current practice, your dissertation research, future – post-DSW – environments, and more broadly, national and global trends. As much as possible, the course will employ a seminar format. Course readings were selected to provide rich and stimulating material for spirited dialogue. Guest presenters will provide firsthand experience related to selected course topics. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9240 Leadership
coursedescription: This course will present the evolution of leadership theory beginning with classical trait theories and ultimately focusing on more modern perspectives such as adaptive, authentic, and shared leadership models that engage more critical understanding of traditional leadership theory. Ultimately, we frame leadership as a social-constructed, collective experience that is generated by complex group dynamics. We will examine leadership in non-profit organizations, government, and social movements. Readings will include a formal overview of leadership theory as well as contemporary feminist, cultural, and futurist perspectives. The practice focus is on developing new relational capabilities that include deep listening, self-reflection, and adaptive problem interpretation. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Welfare (DSW) students. Spring

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Welfare (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9250 Supervision
coursedescription: Supervision is foundational to social work practice. It is a source of education and support in the profession’s practice as well as during the pursuit of the BSW/MSW degree and clinical licensure. While the profession holds up supervision as an essential component of ethical and effective practice, there is little provided by way of training or education of clinical supervision on social work practice. This course will explore the structure, practice and barriers to providing supervision in an agency/organizational setting. The course material explores the changing context of supervision in the social work field, highlights supervision as a means to teach clinical material, support supervisees impacted by organizational dynamics, and spotlight strategies for managing compassion fatigue, secondary trauma, and burnout in the context of social work practice. This course will invite you to think about the role of clinical supervision in your career and your own style and model preference. The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students. Spring 1 Course Unit

notes: The course is restricted to Doctorate in Clinical Social Work (DSW) students.

coursename: SWRK 9900 DSW Dissertation
coursedescription: All students on dissertation status are registered for year-long dissertation status courses. These courses will receive a temporary mark of PR in the fall to indicate the course is in progress and a permanent mark of S (satisfactory progress) or U (unsatisfactory) at the end of the spring semester (or fall semester if that is the student’s last enrolled term). The mark will be a reflection of the evaluation of the student’s progress based, in part, on the student’s Annual Progress Report. Fall, Spring, and Summer Terms
